math_checks.outcome: Checked the p13 question in the ordinary category of small groupoids with all functors, without an outside source. For a subgroup H of a group G, the inclusion BH -> BG of one-object groupoids is monic because it is injective on the sole object and on arrows. If a classifier 1 -> Omega existed, a classifying functor BG -> Omega for this nonempty subobject would send the sole object of BG to the truth object. The pullback on arrows would therefore be the kernel of the induced homomorphism G -> Aut_Omega(truth), hence a normal subgroup. Taking G = S_3 and H = {1,(12)} contradicts this: conjugation by (123) sends (12) to (23), outside H. Thus this ordinary groupoid category has no subobject classifier and cannot be a topos. This checks the mathematical obstruction suggested by the question; it does not identify any extra structure on groupoids or change the printed question or its grammar.
